claims.claim: For d=δ⁺(D)≥1, a directed cycle of length at least d+1 can be found in polynomial time; additionally, n<d+k is an immediate sound NO condition. Thus the target is completely solved for k=1.
claims.evidence: For an inclusion-maximal simple directed path P=v₁…v_p, every out-neighbor of v_p lies among v₁,…,v_{p−1}. If v_i is its earliest out-neighbor, the at least d distinct out-neighbors occupy positions i,…,p−1, so p−i≥d. Hence v_i…v_pv_i is a directed cycle of length p−i+1≥d+1. Greedy extension and selection of i are polynomial. Every cycle has at most n vertices, proving the stated NO test. At k=1 the constructed cycle meets the target.
claims.witness: The closing arc v_p→v_i certifies the cycle v_i→v_{i+1}→…→v_p→v_i.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the universal argument directly and exhaustively checked the greedy construction on every loopless digraph of orders 2–4 with positive minimum outdegree.

claims.claim: For any integer L≥2, existence of a directed cycle of length at least L is exactly equivalent to a short-leg two-way linkage, yielding an explicit O(n^L(n+m)) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: Given an enumerated directed path v₁…v_L and a v_L-to-v₁ path after deleting v₂,…,v_{L−1}, choose the return path simple; its internal vertices are disjoint from the enumerated path, so their union is a simple directed cycle of length at least L. Conversely, L consecutive vertices of any cycle of length at least L form the enumerated path, while the complementary cycle segment supplies the permitted return path. There are fewer than n^L tuples and one O(n+m) reachability test per valid tuple; L>n can be rejected immediately.
claims.witness: The two mutually inverse witnesses are an L-vertex segment plus its internally disjoint return path, and an L-vertex segment of an existing long cycle.
claims.search_method: Proved both implications directly and exhaustively compared the linkage predicate with exact circumference for every loopless digraph of orders 2–4 and every threshold 2≤L≤n+1.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable upper-bound certificate: if X is an independent vertex set and every arc entering X from outside X has its tail in S⊆V(D)\X, then every directed cycle has length at most n−|X|+|S|.
claims.evidence: For each x∈C∩X, independence puts its predecessor on C outside X, and the entering-arc condition puts that predecessor in S. Different x have different predecessors because a vertex has only one successor on the directed cycle. Thus |C∩X|≤|C∩S|≤|S|, while C contains at most n−|X| vertices outside X. Adding gives |C|≤n−|X|+|S|. Independence and the entering-arc condition are directly checkable in polynomial time.
claims.witness: The injective map x↦the predecessor of x on C maps C∩X into C∩S.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the injection proof and exhaustively tested all admissible X,S certificates on every loopless digraph of orders 2–4.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥3 there are 2-strong NO-instances of arbitrarily large order with n≥d+k and circumference exactly d+k−1.
claims.evidence: Set r=k−1 and take the complete bidirected bipartite digraph with parts R,A of sizes r and a≥k. Since r≥2, deleting one vertex leaves both parts nonempty, and the remaining digraph is strong. Degrees are a on R and r on A, so d=r. Every directed cycle alternates between the parts and therefore has length at most 2r; using all R and any r vertices of A attains 2r=d+k−1. Also n=r+a≥2k−1=d+k, and increasing a gives arbitrary order.
claims.witness: R={r₁,…,r_r}, A containing a₁,…,a_r, with cycle r₁a₁r₂a₂…r_ra_rr₁.
claims.search_method: Checked the quantifiers and formulas symbolically, then exactly computed degrees, deletion-connectivity, and circumference for six representative instances with 3≤k≤5.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4 there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and with n≥d+k; indeed their circumference is exactly d+3.
claims.evidence: In the stated construction, vertices of Q\{x,y} have outdegree q−1, A-vertices have outdegree q, and x,y have outdegree q−1+a, giving d=q−1. After any single deletion, a complete surviving core remains and at least one of x,y remains as a gate from the core to A; arcs A→Q provide the reverse direction, proving 2-strongness. Each A-vertex on a cycle has distinct predecessor x or y, so at most two occur and the circumference is at most q+2. The displayed cycle uses all q core vertices and two A-vertices, attaining q+2=d+3. Taking a≥k−1 gives n≥d+k, and unbounded q gives unbounded d.
claims.witness: For Q\{x,y} ordered as z₁,…,z_{q−2}, the cycle x→a₁→z₁→…→z_{q−2}→y→a₂→x has length q+2.
claims.search_method: Checked all deletion cases and the predecessor bound symbolically, then exactly computed twelve representative instances for k∈{4,5}, 3≤q≤5, and a∈{k−1,k}.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4, there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and order, with n≥d+k and circumference exactly d+k−1.
claims.evidence: Let s=k−2≥2. With a bidirected q-core Q, gate set S of size s, independent A, arcs A→Q and S→A, the three outdegrees are q−1 on Q\S, q on A, and q−1+a on S. Since q≥s+1, d=q−1. After one deletion at least one gate and at least one core vertex remain, so every surviving core vertex reaches A through a gate and every A-vertex reaches the core directly; hence the graph is 2-strong. Applying claim 2 with X=A bounds every cycle by q+s. A cycle containing every core vertex and s A-vertices attains q+s=(q−1)+k−1=d+k−1. Since a≥k−1, n=q+a≥d+k. Independently increasing q and a yields unbounded minimum outdegree and order.
claims.witness: With S={s₁,…,s_s} and Q\S={t₁,…,t_{q−s}}, use s₁→a₁→s₂→a₂→…→s_s→a_s→t₁→…→t_{q−s}→s₁.
claims.search_method: Verified degree, connectivity, upper-bound, attaining-cycle, and order formulas symbolically, then exactly computed eight representative instances for k∈{4,5}.

claims.claim: The target has a polynomial-time solution on semicomplete digraphs: such an input is YES exactly when n≥d+k, and a Hamiltonian directed cycle can be constructed when YES.
claims.evidence: The cycle-expansion proof is complete. If an outside z cannot be inserted into C, then c_i→z forces, by non-insertability and semicompleteness, c_{i+1}→z and not z→c_{i+1}; iterating around C makes z strictly dominated by all of C. If no c_i→z exists, semicompleteness makes z strictly dominate all of C. Thus outside vertices split into the two claimed classes. If either class were empty, strongness would fail in one direction. A path from a C-dominated vertex to C must contain an arc u→v from the dominated class to the dominating class. Then c_i→u→v→c_{i+1} expands C by two vertices; a directly insertable vertex expands it by one. Repetition is polynomial and ends with a Hamiltonian cycle. Therefore a 2-strong semicomplete input has a cycle of length d+k exactly when the necessary order condition n≥d+k holds.
claims.witness: At a stalled cycle, an arc u→v from the C-dominated class to the C-dominating class permits replacement of any cycle edge c_i→c_{i+1} by c_i→u→v→c_{i+1}.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the expansion invariant and all stalled cases, then enumerated all 59,808 semicomplete digraphs of orders 2–5 and successfully constructed Hamiltonian cycles in all 52,528 strong ones.

target_evidence: The source target requires an f(k)n^{O(1)} algorithm for arbitrary 2-strong digraphs. The draft does not supply one: the general exact algorithm has exponent L=d+k, the semicomplete algorithm applies only to a proper subclass, and the certificates and obstruction families are structural results rather than an FPT algorithm. These are correct and material partial advances, and the writeup expressly states that the general target remains unresolved, so its PARTIAL claim is accurate.
checks_performed: Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json; used no web or other evidence, retrieval, arm, prompt, or prior-run material.

Independently reconstructed every universal proof, including the maximal-path closure, linkage equivalence, predecessor injection, every deletion case in the obstruction families, and the stalled-cycle cases in the semicomplete construction.

Created and ran the exact finite checker /work/audit_tcs_directed_cycle_attempt2.py; it checked 4,164 general digraphs, 2,429 maximal-path cases, 16,584 linkage cases, 131,755 valid certificate cases, 26 obstruction instances, and all semicomplete digraphs through order five, ending with all_exact_checks_passed.
